zones.label: Solar Night Light
zones.summary: An autonomous light that collects energy by day and turns on after dark.
facts: Core parts: Solar panel, rechargeable cell, charge/protection circuit, light sensor, LED, and enclosure.
Design challenge: Balance harvested energy, battery capacity, LED brightness, and weather protection.
Best fit: A moderate project for learners interested in renewable energy and outdoor electronics.

zones.label: Interactive Busy Board
zones.summary: A tactile panel where switches and knobs produce lights, sounds, or motion.
facts: Core parts: Multiple input controls, LEDs or actuators, power distribution, and a durable enclosure.
Design challenge: Make every interaction understandable, safe, strain-relieved, and satisfying.
Best fit: A moderate-to-advanced project for learners who enjoy interface design and many small circuits.

zones.label: LED Noodle Wearable
zones.summary: A wearable light project that turns flexible LED tubing into a bold visual pattern.
facts: Core parts: LED noodle or flexible light, battery, switch, current-control or driver circuit, and garment attachments.
Design challenge: Keep wiring flexible, insulated, lightweight, and comfortable while managing battery runtime.
Best fit: A beginner-to-moderate project blending electronics, fashion, and event lighting.

quiz.question: Which project must balance daytime energy harvesting with nighttime battery use?
quiz.explanation: The solar night light is an energy-budget and outdoor-enclosure challenge.

quiz.question: Which project emphasizes many tactile inputs and immediate feedback?
quiz.explanation: A busy board combines switches, knobs, lights, and other responses.

quiz.question: Which project makes flexibility, comfort, and portable power central design constraints?
quiz.explanation: Wearable lighting must move safely and comfortably with the garment.
